mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.1% indicates ultra-accommodative monetary policy, which compresses discount rates for equity valuation and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.1% (t-test p > 0.05 vs baseline positive return rate).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% signals labor market deterioration, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced consumer spending capacity.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0 (t-test p > 0.05 vs negative return expectation).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in residential construction (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) signals robust economic activity, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of HOUST and INDPRO increasing fails to produce positive returns in more than 60% of cases (t-test p > 0.05 vs positive return rate).

mechanism_narrative: During high inflation periods (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% year-over-year), the Federal Reserve typically initiates monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% (t-test p > 0.05 vs negative return expectation).

mechanism_narrative: A rising GDP growth rate (GDPC1) indicates expanding economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to improved corporate earnings prospects.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 growth is positive (t-test p > 0.05 vs positive return expectation).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment increase exceeding 200,000 persons signals strong labor market conditions, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to rising consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS > 200000 (t-test p > 0.05 vs positive return expectation).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a tightening monetary cycle and labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of UNRATE rising and FEDFUNDS rising fails to produce negative returns in more than 60% of cases (t-test p > 0.05 vs negative return expectation).

mechanism_narrative: In periods of strong consumer spending (RSAFS > 500,000 million dollars), the S&P 500 typically produces positive returns over the next 20 trading days due to elevated corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS > 500000 (t-test p > 0.05 vs positive return expectation).
